events.text:
I just forked this repo (AERIS-10, an open-source 10.5 GHz pulse-LFM phased-array radar) and I want to use it to LEARN how a phased-array radar is designed and implemented end to end. Give me a guided technical tour — not a code review, not a contribution.

About me: intermediate embedded dev, comfortable with C, STM32/ESP32, and basic Verilog; math through Calc 2; new to RF and radar DSP. I learn best from "here's the concept → here's where it lives in the code → here's the math I'd need to go deeper."

Important context: this repo is tagged pre-bringup/alpha — the hardware has reportedly never been powered on. The README is polished and heavily marketed, and GitHub reports a large fraction of the codebase as PL/SQL, which makes no sense for a radar project. So be skeptical and empirical: verify claims against the actual files, and tell me plainly what's real engineering vs. boilerplate, auto-generated filler, stubs, or aspirational README copy the code doesn't back up.

Work in stages, and STOP after Stage 1 to show me the map and your plan before going deep:

Stage 1 — Map it. Walk the directory tree. For each top-level folder, tell me what's actually in it and the real file types — use shell tools (file, find, wc -l, grep) rather than trusting filenames. Resolve the PL/SQL mystery: what are those files really? End with one honest paragraph on how much of this is substantive vs. padding.

Stage 2 — The signal chain. Trace the end-to-end radar path: waveform generation → up-conversion → TX beamforming/array → target → RX → down-conversion → ADC → FPGA. Tie each stage to the actual part numbers and where they appear in the schematics/BOM. Give a short intuition for each RF concept (LFM chirp, mixing/IF, phase-shift beam steering).

Stage 3 — The FPGA DSP. Open the Verilog. Tell me what's ACTUALLY implemented vs. merely claimed: is there real RTL for pulse compression, Doppler FFT, MTI, and CFAR — or placeholders? For each stage that exists, explain what the DSP does conceptually and flag the prerequisite math I'd need to truly understand it (where I'd hit Fourier transforms, complex I/Q, or detection theory I don't have yet).

Stage 4 — Firmware + host. How the STM32 firmware orchestrates the system (clock gen, synthesizers, phase shifters, power sequencing, peripheral setup) and talks to the FPGA; then how data flows from the FPGA to the Python GUI.

Output: as you go, build a LEARNING_NOTES.md organized by subsystem, with two standing sections — "Concepts to study next" (the math/EE background I'm missing, in a sensible order) and "Claims vs. reality" (where the repo's pitch outruns its contents). Read and explain only — don't build, synthesize, or flash anything.
I'll start with Stage 1 — mapping the repository empirically. Let me explore the structure with shell tools rather than trusting filenames.

7	# AERIS-10: Open Source Pulse Linear Frequency Modulated Phased Array Radar
8	
9	[![Hardware: CERN-OHL-P](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardware-CERN--OHL--P-blue.svg)](https://ohwr.org/cern_ohl_p_v2.txt)
10	[![Software: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/Software-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
11	[![Status: Alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Alpha-orange)](https://github.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR)
12	[![Features: Work in Progress](https://img.shields.io/badge/Features-Work_in_Progress-yellow)](https://github.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR/issues)
13	[![Frequency: 10.5GHz](https://img.shields.io/badge/Frequency-10.5GHz-blue)](https://github.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR)
14	[![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR/pulls)
15	
16	
17	AERIS-10 is an open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz phased array radar system featuring Pulse Linear Frequency Modulated (LFM) modulation. Available in two versions (3km and 20km range), it's designed for researchers, drone developers, and serious SDR enthusiasts who want to explore and experiment with phased array radar technology.
18	
19	![AERIS-10 Antenna Array](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR/main/8_Utils/Antenna_Array.jpg)
20	
21	## 📡 Overview
22	
23	The AERIS-10 project aims to democratize radar technology by providing a fully open-source, modular, and hackable radar system. Whether you're a university researcher, a drone startup, or an advanced maker, AERIS-10 offers a platform for experimenting with beamforming, pulse compression, Doppler processing, and target tracking.
24	
25	## 🔬 Key Features
26	
27	- **Open Source Hardware & Software** - Complete schematics, PCB layouts, firmware, and software available
28	- **Dual Version Availability**:
29	  - **AERIS-10N (Nexus)**: 3km range with 8x16 patch antenna array
30	  - **AERIS-10E (Extended)**: 20km range with 32x16 dielectric-filled slotted waveguide array
31	- **Full Electronic Beam Steering** - ±45° electronic steering in elevation and azimuth
32	- **Advanced Signal Processing** - On-board FPGA handles pulse compression, Doppler FFT, MTI, and CFAR
33	- **Python GUI** - User-friendly interface with map integration
34	- **GPS/IMU Integration** - Real-time position and attitude correction
35	- **Modular Design** - Separate power management, frequency synthesis, and RF boards
36	
37	## 🏗️ System Architecture
38	
39	![AERIS-10 System Diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NawfalMotii79/PLFM_RADAR/main/8_Utils/RADAR_V6_V2.png)
40	
41	### Hardware Components
42	
43	The AERIS-10 main sub-systems are:
44	
45	- **Power Management Board** - Supplies all necessary voltage levels to the electronics components with proper filtering and sequencing (sequencing ensured by the microcontroller)
46	
47	- **Frequency Synthesizer Board** - Uses a high-performance Low Jitter Clock Generator (AD9523-1) that supplies phase-aligned clock references for:
48	  - RX and TX Frequency Synthesizers (ADF4382)
49	  - DAC
50	  - ADC
51	  - FPGA
52	
53	- **Main Board** containing:
54	  - **DAC** - Generates the RADAR Chirps
55	  - **2x Microwave Mixers (LTC5552)** - For up-conversion and IF-down-conversion
56	  - **4x 4-Channel Phase Shifters (ADAR1000)** -…[truncated for dataset]
